newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia to sell ailing white goods firm.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia to sell ailing white goods firm.

text.p: Tunisia on Monday launched an international tender to sell household utilities firm Electro-Menager de Tunisie, an ailing firm privatised in 1990.
The tender was signed by a superintendent named by a Ben Arous court which placed the firm under judicial administration in a ruling dated March 27 this year.
Electro-Menager de Tunisie, known as Le Confort before privatisation, was assembling mainly refrigerators and stoves at its plant at Ben Arous, near Tunis.

In one of the first Tunisian privatisations, it was sold in 1990 to a group of Tunisian private businessmen led by Afif Kilani for 3.3 million dinars. It had a 40 million dinars deficit when it was privatised.

Meanwhile, other private investors entered the country's household market, including Whirlpool Corp and Turkish Arcelik, giving the Tunisian firm tough competition until it stopped production last year.
No financial results were published in recent years, but industry sources said its debt was over 40 million dinars.
The tender's notice says the firm was to be sold "globally and with all its elements" by June 15, 1997. ($=1.09 dinar)
